subject: literature
passage: Aunt Ruth had lost most of her sight the winter Theo turned eleven, and she said the hardest part was not the dark but the way the neighborhood had gone silent in her mind. So Theo made her a map. He walked the eight blocks between her apartment and the park with a notebook, writing down the clatter of the bakery's shutters at six, the bus that sighed at the corner, the loose grate outside the laundry that rang when anyone stepped on ______ read it to her every Sunday, and by the end of the month she could tell him exactly who was passing below.
stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

explanation.why: "He walked the eight blocks … writing down the clatter … the loose grate … that rang when anyone stepped on it" is a complete sentence, and "he read it to her every Sunday" begins another. Two independent clauses need a strong boundary between them, and a semicolon provides one.
explanation.A: Incorrect. A comma alone cannot join two independent clauses; this creates a comma splice.
explanation.B: Incorrect. With no punctuation, the two independent clauses run together (a run-on sentence).
explanation.C: Incorrect. When "and" joins two independent clauses, a comma is needed before it; here the missing comma also makes it seem that the grate rang whenever he read.
explanation.D: Correct. A semicolon correctly joins the two independent clauses.
